drhp.business: Bikaji manufactures and sells premium Indian ethnic snacks and packaged foods under the 'Bikaji' brand, introduced in 1993, which reflects the culture, flavours and culinary heritage of Bikaner. Its offerings span six principal categories, from its flagship Bikaneri Bhujia to namkeen, packaged sweets, papad, western snacks and other snacks, catering to evolving consumer preferences and diverse consumption occasions. risks.note: Management explicitly flagged that FY2025-26 growth was achieved 'despite temporary volatility in commodity prices that exerted upward pressure on our input costs' — an agri-linked snack portfolio leaves gross margin exposed to input-cost swings.
risks.risk: Commodity / raw-material price volatility pressuring input costs

risks.note: The 50:50 joint venture with Chaudhary Group approved on July 23, 2025 requires co-investing in a new state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in a new country; it is described as 'a cornerstone of our long-term global strategy', so delays, partner alignment or local-market missteps would set back the international agenda.
risks.risk: Execution and partner risk in the Nepal joint venture

risks.note: The 70:30 joint venture with Mr. Thayekunni Khaleel of 'Bakemart' approved November 11, 2025 takes the Company into the 'rapidly expanding bakery category', where returns depend on integrating a partner's manufacturing and product-innovation capability with Bikaji's distribution.
risks.risk: Diversification into an adjacent category (bakery) outside the core ethnic-snacks competence

risks.note: The Company has entered the QSR space and plans additional outlets after its first launch; a fresh-food, store-level operating model carries different working-capital, site-selection and operating-cost dynamics than packaged-snacks manufacturing.
risks.risk: New business-model risk from entering the Quick Service Restaurant (QSR) format

risks.note: Growth is anchored on brand strength — a refreshed corporate identity rolled out across packaging, communication materials and customer touchpoints, and the celebrity-led 'Kya Baat Hai Ji!' campaign — so brand missteps or campaign under-delivery directly affect the growth narrative.
risks.risk: Dependence on brand equity and marketing execution

risks.note: Uttar Pradesh is called 'a vital frontier' for the 'Har Ghar Bikaji' vision and is described as a region with 'a rich legacy of namkeen', implying entrenched local and regional competition in the markets Bikaji is targeting for incremental growth.
risks.risk: New-geography penetration risk in competitive namkeen markets

risks.note: The Company's own forward-looking statement caution notes that such statements 'are subject to risks and opportunities beyond the Company's control' and that 'there is no guarantee that future results will be achieved as envisaged'.
risks.risk: Forward-looking plans subject to factors outside the Company's control
